description: Single-shot LLM agent with MCP tool support, using the Anthropic SDK directly (no LiteLLM dependency). Runs a tool-calling loop until the model returns a final answer or max_iterations.

outputs.description: Agent run dict: {final_answer, iterations, tool_calls_made, tool_call_details, transcript, stopped_reason, model, mcp_servers}

mcp_servers.label: MCP Servers
mcp_servers.description: MCP servers to expose as tools. Each entry is declared inline (name + transport fields) or shared via server_resource_key (an MCPServerResource component's resource_key) -- exactly one of the two per entry.

name.description: Short name used to prefix tool names. Required when declaring the server inline; leave unset when using server_resource_key.

server_resource_key.description: Resource key of an MCPServerResource component to use instead of declaring this server inline -- lets several agent components share one registered server. Exactly one of `name` (inline spec) or `server_resource_key` is required.

instructions.description: Free-text usage guidance for this server -- appended to the system prompt under a heading with the server's name, combined with whatever `instructions` the MCP server itself returns in its own initialize response, if it sets one.

asset_tags.label: Asset Tags
asset_tags.description: Additional key-value tags applied to the asset in the Dagster catalog.

deps.label: Deps
deps.description: Lineage-only upstream asset keys (no data passed at runtime).

thinking_budget.label: Thinking Budget
thinking_budget.description: Max reasoning-trace tokens for Claude thinking mode (claude-opus-4.1+, claude-sonnet-4+). When set, Anthropic returns a `thinking` block alongside the visible answer showing the model's reasoning trace. Cost implication: thinking tokens are billed as output tokens. Leave None (default) for standard non-thinking behavior.

prompt_caching.label: Prompt Caching
prompt_caching.description: Anthropic prompt caching. When true, wraps the system prompt with `cache_control: {type: ephemeral}`. First call warms the cache (~25% surcharge on that call); subsequent calls within ~5 min read from cache (~90% cheaper on the cached prefix). Big win for long system prompts + MCP tool schemas that repeat across pipeline runs OR across loop iterations.

kinds.description: Asset kinds shown in the Dagster catalog (e.g. snowflake, python). Auto-inferred from component name if empty.
kinds.label: Kinds

partition_type.description: Enable partitioning: 'daily', 'weekly', 'monthly', 'hourly' for time-based; 'static' for a fixed set of values (e.g. customers); 'multi' for date × static (e.g. day × customer). Leave empty for unpartitioned.
partition_type.label: Partition Type

partition_cron_schedule.label: Partition Cron Schedule
partition_cron_schedule.description: Required when partition_type='cron'. A cron expression restricting the date axis to a custom cadence, e.g. '0 0 * * 1-5' for weekdays only (business-day cadence). Built on Dagster's TimeWindowPartitionsDefinition(cron_schedule=...).

partition_cron_fmt.label: Partition Cron Fmt
partition_cron_fmt.description: strftime format for partition keys produced by partition_type='cron'. Only change this for a sub-daily cron_schedule.

partition_end_offset.label: Partition End Offset
partition_end_offset.description: Passed through to the underlying Daily/Weekly/Monthly/Hourly/cron partitions definition. 0 (the Dagster default) means a time-based partition set only ever holds COMPLETED windows -- e.g. a daily set never includes today until tomorrow. Set to 1 to include the current, still-in-progress window.

partition_timezone.label: Partition Timezone
partition_timezone.description: IANA timezone for the underlying Daily/Weekly/Monthly/Hourly/cron partitions definition (defaults to UTC when unset, matching Dagster's own default).

partition_start.description: ISO date string for the first partition, e.g. '2024-01-01'. Required for time-based and multi partition types.
partition_start.label: Partition Start Date

partition_values.description: Comma-separated values for static or multi partitioning, e.g. 'acme_corp,globex,initech'. Required for static and multi types.
partition_values.label: Partition Values

partition_dimensions.description: Multi-axis partition spec: list of {name, type, start, values, dynamic_partition_name} dicts. Overrides flat fields when set.
partition_dimensions.label: Partition Dimensions

freshness_max_lag_minutes.description: Maximum acceptable lag in minutes before this asset is considered stale.
freshness_max_lag_minutes.label: Freshness Max Lag (minutes)

freshness_cron.description: Cron schedule for the freshness policy, e.g. '0 9 * * 1-5' (weekdays 9am).
freshness_cron.label: Freshness Cron Schedule

retry_policy_max_retries.description: Max retries on asset failure. Defines a RetryPolicy. Useful for transient network failures, rate limits, etc.
retry_policy_max_retries.label: Retry Policy Max Retries

skill_keys.label: Skill Keys
skill_keys.description: SkillResource resource_keys (from SkillResourceComponent) to make available to this agent. Each listed skill's name/description go into the agent's context up front; the full SKILL.md only loads if the agent actually calls load_skill.

allowed_tools.label: Allowed Tools
allowed_tools.description: Optional allowlist of namespaced tool names (e.g. 'dagster_plus__list_runs'), '*' wildcards supported (fnmatch), applied across every mcp_servers entry. Default: all discovered tools. A server can expose many tools the agent shouldn't be able to call (e.g. a hosted Dagster+ MCP server's terminate_run/rerun_run/delete_alert_policy alongside read-only ones) -- this is the lever to restrict an agent to a safe subset, e.g. ['dagster_plus__list_*', 'dagster_plus__get_*'].

code_execution_tool_version.label: Code Execution Tool Version
code_execution_tool_version.description: Tool `type` string for the code execution tool hosted_skills enables -- 'code_execution_20250825' (the broadly-supported default) or a later version (e.g. 'code_execution_20260120'/'code_execution_20260521') for programmatic tool calling or REPL state persistence. No anthropic-beta header is needed for any of these -- confirmed against Anthropic's own current docs, not the older, now-unnecessary beta header some earlier guidance mentioned.

hosted_skills_files_dir.label: Hosted Skills Files Dir
hosted_skills_files_dir.description: Local directory root -- hosted_skills only. When set, every file Claude's code execution generates is ALSO written here (one subfolder per dagster/run_id, a manifest.json per run) in the exact same shape report_tools_server uses -- so slack_reply/teams_reply's own report_files_dir (and slack_chat_tools' upload_files) deliver these files with zero changes needed there. Point it at the SAME directory if you want generated files from both report_tools_server and hosted_skills delivered through one report_files_dir.

hosted_skills.label: Hosted Skills
hosted_skills.description: Skills Claude runs with CODE EXECUTION in Anthropic's hosted sandbox -- a different, separate mechanism from skill_keys. Each entry is a built-in skill (type: anthropic, skill_id: pdf/docx/xlsx/pptx) or a custom one, referenced either literally (type + skill_id) or via skill_resource_key (a SkillResourceComponent with publish_as_custom_skill: true).

type.description: 'anthropic' for a built-in skill, 'custom' for one uploaded via the Skills API. Required together with skill_id; leave both unset when using skill_resource_key instead.

skill_id.description: The skill id -- a built-in name ('pdf'/'docx'/'xlsx'/'pptx') when type='anthropic', or an uploaded skill_id when type='custom'. Required together with type.

skill_resource_key.description: Resource key of a SkillResourceComponent with publish_as_custom_skill: true -- resolved to that skill anthropic_skill_id at run time. Alternative to type+skill_id.

version.description: Skill version, or 'latest' (default) for the most recent.

outcome_ledger_path.label: Outcome Ledger Path
outcome_ledger_path.description: Directory a ledger-aware tool server (github_pr_tools/linear_ticket_tools, its own ledger_path field pointed at this SAME directory) writes this run's consequential actions into, keyed by run_id -- read by the companion outcome asset (see emit_outcome_asset). Unset: the outcome asset still emits (when enabled), just with empty filed/would_file/refused/decisions_for_you.

decisions_marker.label: Decisions Marker
decisions_marker.description: Heading (case-insensitive) that starts the agent's 'decisions for a person' section at the end of its final answer. The lines under it fill the outcome asset's decisions_for_you ("none" gives nothing), and the answer text before it becomes the outcome's `summary` metadata (700 chars). Empty disables both.

emit_outcome_asset.label: Emit Outcome Asset
emit_outcome_asset.description: Build a companion '{asset_name}_outcome' asset (same partitions_def as this asset) that collapses this run's outcome-ledger entries (see outcome_ledger_path) plus this asset's own final_answer into {status, filed, would_file, refused, decisions_for_you, text} -- matched by run_id, not a wall-clock time window (which mixes concurrent runs together). Shaped to feed agent_fixture_check directly.

on_required_tool_calls_missing.label: On Required Tool Calls Missing
on_required_tool_calls_missing.description: What happens when required_tool_calls is set and still unsatisfied after the one reminder. 'fail' (default) raises, so the run fails and the reason is in the run's own failure message -- turns 'did it act' into a guarantee instead of a hope. 'warn' never raises; the result (and the materialization's own metadata) instead carries required_tools_missing, the list of entries that were never satisfied (empty list when everything required was called).

context_notes.label: Context Notes
context_notes.description: Free text appended to the system prompt under its own heading, naming what's deliberate in the repo/environment this agent reviews -- a demo's artificial flakiness, a test fixture that's supposed to fail, a known limitation that isn't a bug. Without this, an advisor agent has filed 'fix' findings against exactly the things a repo was built to demonstrate. Not a substitute for reading the repo's own README/CONTRIBUTING first (put that instruction in the prompt or system_prompt instead) -- this is for the handful of things worth saying explicitly even after that, or when no such doc exists.
